headline: OpenAI Ships a Codex Plugin Directly Into Claude Code
lede: On March 30, 2026, OpenAI released an open-source plugin that lets developers invoke its Codex coding agent from within Claude Code without leaving their terminal. The move marks the first time a major AI lab has shipped official tooling into a direct rival's platform — and into one that, by early 2026, had quietly claimed an estimated $2.5 billion in annualized revenue and roughly 4 percent of all public GitHub commits.
body:
The plugin, published as openai/codex-plugin-cc under the Apache-2.0 license, accumulated 17,800 stars within weeks. Romain Huet, OpenAI's Head of Developer Experience, framed the release in plainly generous terms: “We love an open ecosystem.” That framing sits alongside reporting that OpenAI's CEO of Applications Fidji Simo privately described Claude Code's rise as a “wake-up call,” a detail that gives the plugin a second reading as competitive retaliation by other means.

Technically, the plugin is a thin but capable wrapper around two components OpenAI open-sourced earlier in 2026: the **Codex harness** — the agent loop and reasoning logic underlying every Codex surface — and the *Codex app server*, a bidirectional *JSON-RPC 2.0* interface written largely in Rust that decouples that harness from any specific client. The plugin calls the codex binary already on the developer's machine and bundles no separate runtime. Three primary *slash commands* are exposed: /codex:review for a read-only pass over uncommitted changes, /codex:adversarial-review for a devil's-advocate challenge of design choices, and /codex:rescue to hand an unresolved task off to Codex in the background. During review passes, Codex dispatches up to four parallel sub-agents.

The plugin's most distinctive feature is the *Review Gate*: an optional Claude Code *stop hook* that intercepts the model's output before a turn completes, submits it to Codex for a targeted review, and — if Codex surfaces issues — blocks Claude from finishing and forces a correction cycle. The result is a self-reinforcing quality loop in which one model automatically audits the other's work. OpenAI warns the gate can be expensive and recommends enabling it only during monitored sessions; an open issue notes the stop hook occasionally fails due to a state-directory resolution bug.

The strategic context matters. Claude Code controls an estimated 4 percent of public GitHub commits by early 2026, making Anthropic the dominant player in agentic coding. By shipping into Claude Code's plugin marketplace — an OpenAI repository installable directly via Anthropic's own directory — OpenAI reaches its rival's most engaged users without asking them to switch surfaces. The play is ecosystem penetration rather than direct substitution.

The plugin arrives amid a broader industry shift away from platform lock-in. OpenAI, Anthropic, Block (SQ), Google (GOOGL), Microsoft (MSFT), and others co-founded the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation to standardize cross-agent interoperability, anchored by Anthropic's *Model Context Protocol* (MCP), Block's Goose, and OpenAI's AGENTS.md specification. Anthropic's Agent Skills standard was adopted within 48 hours by 32 competing tools, including products from Amazon (AMZN) Web Services and Microsoft. The Codex plugin is, in that light, less a novelty than a specimen of a new normal: AI vendors building deliberately into each other's dominant surfaces.

concepts.definition: The core agent loop and reasoning engine underlying all Codex experiences — CLI, VS Code extension, web app, and third-party plugins. It handles planning, tool use, and multi-step task execution, and is the component that performs actual code generation and editing.

A bidirectional JSON-RPC 2.0 interface, written largely in Rust, that decouples the Codex harness from any specific client surface. It organizes conversations into threads, turns, and items; streams real-time notifications to clients; and provides approval gating for sensitive operations. Open-sourced by OpenAI in early 2026.

A lightweight remote procedure call protocol that encodes requests and responses as JSON objects. Version 2.0 supports both request-response and notification patterns, making it well-suited for streaming agent updates. The Codex app server uses it as its primary transport layer.

An optional quality-control mechanism in the Codex plugin for Claude Code. When enabled, a stop hook intercepts Claude's output before a turn completes, submits it to Codex for review, and blocks Claude from finishing if Codex finds problems — forcing Claude to address the issues before the session ends.

A Claude Code lifecycle hook that executes when the model is about to complete a turn and emit its final output. Hooks can inspect and block the stop event, allowing external tools to gate Claude's completion on custom conditions such as a passing code review.

A user-invocable command in Claude Code prefixed with a forward slash, such as /codex:review. Slash commands are exposed by installed plugins and skills, and execute predefined workflows — in this case, triggering a Codex review or background task delegation.

An open standard originally developed by Anthropic that defines how AI agents expose and consume tools across different platforms and clients. MCP servers publish callable tools over a standardized protocol that any MCP-aware client can discover and invoke, enabling interoperability between AI systems from different vendors.

A Linux Foundation project co-founded by OpenAI, Anthropic, Block, Google, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, and others to standardize interoperability infrastructure for AI agents. It is organized around three open-source pillars: Anthropic's MCP, Block's Goose, and OpenAI's AGENTS.md specification.

An open standard introduced by Anthropic that allows AI tools to publish reusable, invocable capabilities — slash commands, hooks, agents — in a portable SKILL.md format. Within 48 hours of its launch in early 2026, 32 competing tools had adopted it, including offerings from Google, Microsoft, and Amazon Web Services.

A permissive open-source software license that allows users to freely use, modify, and distribute the software, including in proprietary products, provided that the original license and attribution notices are preserved. It is among the most business-friendly open-source licenses.

repos.summary: The official OpenAI plugin for Claude Code, enabling developers to invoke Codex for code review, adversarial review, and background task delegation from within a Claude Code session. Exposes slash commands and an optional Review Gate stop hook. Apache-2.0 licensed, it reached 17,800 stars within weeks of its March 2026 release.

OpenAI's open-source Codex repository, containing the CLI, SDK, and Codex app server written primarily in Rust. The app server exposes the Codex harness as a JSON-RPC 2.0 interface that third-party clients — including codex-plugin-cc — can integrate against. Over 80,000 stars as of early 2026.

thread_summary: Romain Huet opened the thread by noting that Claude Code users had already been reaching for Codex independently — for code review and for more complex tasks — and framed the plugin as a natural formalization of a workflow that was already emerging. The bookmarked follow-up highlights that the plugin is architecturally grounded in the same open-source Codex app server and harness used by OpenAI's own first-party tools, giving it the same parallel-tasking and review capabilities rather than a bespoke, lightweight bridge.
